data.name: Qatar
data.summary: Territorial system with no tax on employment income and no tax on capital gains, dividends, interest or rent for individuals who do not carry on a taxable business activity in Qatar. Gains on Qatari real estate and securities are exempt for residents unless part of a taxable activity (non-residents pay 10% on Qatar-source gains). No inheritance, gift or wealth tax; no VAT yet (a draft VAT law has been approved by the Cabinet but not published). Corporate tax 10% on foreign-owned profits; 15% DMTT/IIR for large MNEs from 2025. About 83 treaties, none with the US. Property purchase of QAR 3.65m+ in designated areas gives permanent-residency benefits.

regimes.name: Qatar tax residence
regimes.description: No tax on individuals' investment income or gains; territorial system.
regimes.eligibility: Any legal resident; no special status required.

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax for resident individuals on real estate or securities not held as part of a taxable activity in Qatar.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Non-residents are taxed at 10% on Qatar-source capital gains. A capital gains return is due within 30 days of a sale where tax applies. A business 'activity' is broadly defined (including exploitation of movable or immovable property), so an individual running a Qatar business could be taxed at 10% on its income.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Qatar income tax is territorial; PwC: gains on disposal of real estate and securities are exempt unless part of a taxable activity. Foreign gains are outside the territorial scope.
capital_gains.professional_trader: An individual whose dealing amounts to a taxable 'activity' in Qatar would be taxed at 10% on that Qatar-source business income; passive portfolio investment is not taxed.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign-source gains are outside the territorial scope.

dividends.summary: No tax on dividends for individuals: dividends from profits already taxed in Qatar or from exempt companies are not taxable, and foreign dividends are outside the territorial scope.

dividends.rate_basis: Territorial system; PwC income determination: dividends not taxable if paid from taxed or exempt profits; bank interest not taxable for individuals without a taxable activity.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends paid by Qatari companies.
dividends.treaty_network: About 83 treaties listed by PwC; no treaty with the United States, so US dividends held directly bear 30% US WHT.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No property tax. Owners pay registration fees on property transfers and landlords pay lease registration fees (rates not verified).

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status (family) law based on Sharia governs inheritance of Muslims, with fixed shares (a son typically takes twice a daughter's share) and at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs. How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (home-country law, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified for this country; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice and hold portfolio assets outside the country or through a structure with a clear governing law.

inheritance.foreign_assets: No tax on any asset, local or foreign.

residency.tax_residency_test: Qatar Tax Law (amended by Law 11/2022): resident if the individual has a permanent home in Qatar, or lives in Qatar more than 183 days (continuous or not) in a year, or is a Qatari national. Residence matters little for individuals because tax is territorial and investment income is untaxed.

corporate.summary: Flat 10% CIT on Qatar-source profits of foreign-owned entities; entities wholly owned by Qatari and resident GCC nationals currently pay no CIT; oil operations at least 35%. DMTT and IIR (Pillar Two) apply for fiscal years from 1 January 2025; no UTPR. No WHT on dividends.
corporate.special_zones: Qatar Financial Centre (QFC) and Qatar Free Zones have separate regimes (not verified in this pass).

income.name: Qatar

income_tax.summary: Qatar taxes no employment income of individuals (salaries, wages and allowances are not taxed regardless of residence). The system is territorial: a self-employed individual may owe income tax on qualifying Qatar-source income, and the PwC page states no personal rates. Social insurance is mandatory for Qatari employees only.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed individuals may be taxed on Qatar-source business income (PwC states no rates; corporate-style 10% applies to foreign-owned profits per the existing jurisdiction file). Foreign-source income from foreign clients is outside the territorial charge. Social insurance applies to Qatari nationals only.

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: no visa-free right to work or settle. Skilled employees are normally recruited by a Qatari employer, which arranges the work permit and residence; no dedicated remote-work or digital-nomad visa was found. Residence for property buyers (QAR 3.65 million and above in designated areas) is described in the existing jurisdiction file.

succession.name: Qatar
succession.summary: Muslims are subject to Sharia fixed shares under the Family Law (Law 22 of 2006). Non-Muslims are reported to be governed by their own law, though courts may take jurisdiction and registering a will is advised. Trusts and foundations exist only inside the Qatar Financial Centre.
succession.reserved_share: Muslims: Sharia fixed shares under Law 22 of 2006 (Family Law); share rules not retrieved.
succession.foreign_law_note: Practitioners report that the Family Law leaves non-Muslims to their own laws and the Civil Code's conflict rule points to the deceased's nationality law. Qatari courts can still take jurisdiction (for example where documents are incomplete or assets are in Qatar), and a guide advises registering a will naming the applicable law. Assets may be frozen until a court certificate is presented.
succession.trust_note: Only in the QFC: QFC Trust Regulations 2007 (amended December 2017: registration, licensed professional trustee, no charitable trusts) and QFC Foundations Regulations (foundation with Council and Enforcer, constitution kept confidential). Onshore Qatari law has no trust law. How onshore courts treat QFC structures over Qatari Muslim estates is not settled in the sources.
open_questions: Article of Law 22/2006 on non-Muslims (art. 286 suggested) not retrieved.
QFC Foundations Regulations year not confirmed.
Onshore treatment of QFC trusts/foundations not sourced.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.

immigration.name: Qatar
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone. EU, US and other passports use the same routes: residence by buying property of at least QAR 730,000 (temporary, tied to the property), or at least QAR 3,650,000 for permanent-residency benefits. The statutory permanent residence card needs about 20 years of residence. No remote-work visa was found. Citizenship is practically closed.
immigration.naturalisation: Not researched from the statute in this pass. Qatari nationality law is very restrictive; the permanent residence card (Law No. 10 of 2018) needs 20 years of legal residence (10 if born in Qatar), enough income, good conduct and Arabic.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: General rule, not verified in this pass: Qatar does not allow dual nationality for naturalised citizens.

routes.name: Real estate residency with permanent-residency benefits (QAR 3,650,000)
routes.summary: Buying property worth at least QAR 3,650,000 (about USD 1 million) gives permanent-residency benefits such as health care, education and investment rights.
routes.requirements: Aqarat: purchase of at least QAR 3,650,000 gives 'permanent residency benefits' (health, education, investment). Qualifying areas, whether a card is issued, renewal and presence rules are not published on the Aqarat page. Secondary sources mention an annual cap of 100 and a 90-day annual stay; they conflict and are unconfirmed. Gulf News (13 Oct 2025) reported the unified platform as to be launched.
routes.physical_presence: Not published; secondary sources say 90 days a year (unconfirmed).
routes.family: Qualifying investments can extend to eligible family members (event page, unconfirmed).
routes.tax_note: Qatar taxes individuals only on local business and employment income; a permit does not by itself create tax residence.

routes.name: Real estate residency (QAR 730,000)
routes.summary: Buying property worth at least QAR 730,000 (about USD 200,000) gives a residence permit tied to owning the property.
routes.requirements: Aqarat: purchase of at least QAR 730,000 gives residency tied to the property. Designated freehold and usufruct zones under Cabinet Resolution 28 of 2020 (secondary source). Gulf News (13 Oct 2025) said the one-stop scheme would be officially launched; validity, renewal and minimum stay are not published on Aqarat. Secondary sources say 1-year renewable while the property is held.
routes.physical_presence: Not published; secondary sources say 90 days a year (unconfirmed).
routes.family: Spouse, children and parents reported (secondary, unconfirmed).
routes.tax_note: A permit does not by itself create tax residence.

routes.name: Permanent residence card (Law No. 10 of 2018)
routes.summary: A card giving most citizen benefits to long-term residents; it takes about 20 years of residence.
routes.requirements: Law No. 10 of 2018 as described by the Ministry of Interior (9 April 2019): 20 years of legal residence if born abroad (10 if born in Qatar), income enough for the family, good conduct, sufficient Arabic. Fee QAR 3,000 at application and QAR 3,000 at collection. Not an investment route; investors generally use the property tiers above.
routes.fees_note: QAR 3,000 on document submission plus QAR 3,000 on collection (MoI, 2019).
routes.physical_presence: Continuous legal residence; details not researched.
routes.tax_note: Qatar has no tax on investment income for individuals.

routes.name: Employer-sponsored work residence
routes.summary: Most expatriates live in Qatar on a work permit and residence permit sponsored by an employer or a Qatar Financial Centre entity.
routes.requirements: Employer applies for the work and residence permit through the Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Labour; exit permit rules were relaxed in recent years. Not researched in detail here.
routes.physical_presence: Residence lapses after 6 months outside Qatar (general rule, not verified).
